lessons.title: Getting rich is a skill, not luck
lessons.key_idea: Seek wealth, meaning assets that earn while you sleep, rather than chasing a salary or status, because wealth creation is a positive-sum game anyone can learn.

lessons.title: Find your specific knowledge
lessons.key_idea: Your edge is knowledge that can't be taught in a classroom, found by following your genuine curiosity toward work that feels like play to you but looks like work to others.

lessons.title: Use leverage that needs no permission
lessons.key_idea: Code and media multiply your effort without anyone's permission, letting one person's work reach millions while they sleep.

lessons.title: Take accountability and build judgment
lessons.key_idea: Putting your name on your work and owning the results earns trust and rewards, and with leverage, good judgment becomes the most valuable skill you can have.

lessons.title: Play long-term games with long-term people
lessons.key_idea: The biggest returns in money, relationships and reputation come from compounding over years with people you trust.

lessons.title: Happiness is a skill you can train
lessons.key_idea: Happiness is mostly a state of peace you can cultivate, and every desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get it.

lessons.title: Wealth and peace both buy freedom
lessons.key_idea: Productize yourself to earn freedom from forced work, and build habits like meditation, reading and exercise to earn freedom from your own restless mind.

plan.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
plan.author: Eric Jorgenson
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's structure and core ideas well, since it is a widely read compilation of Naval Ravikant's tweets, podcasts and essays.
plan.one_liner: A tech investor's hard-won ideas on getting rich without luck and staying happy along the way.
plan.summary: Eric Jorgenson gathered years of Naval Ravikant's tweets, podcast conversations and essays and organized them into one short guide. Naval is an entrepreneur and investor best known for cofounding AngelList. The book has two halves. The first is about wealth. Naval argues that getting rich is a learnable skill, not luck. It comes from owning assets, building specific knowledge that others can't easily copy, using leverage like code and media, and taking accountability for your work. The second half is about happiness. Naval treats happiness as a skill too, built through habits like meditation, reading, exercise and letting go of endless desire. The thread connecting both halves is freedom. Wealth buys freedom from having to work. Inner peace frees you from your own restless mind.
